doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: Forgetting your own songs
summary: Musicians forget sessions and songs they do not perform; he has about three hundred songs.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well it’s like people like Bucky Pizzarelli for instance, you’ll find a fact about him. For instance that he played on Ben E. King’s “Stand By Me” and you’ll tell him that and he’ll go, “I did?”
So many sessions and you can’t remember everything.

Well and you know the songs that you remember most, obviously, are the ones that you tend to perform. A lot of times you know you’ll write a song and then you’ll record it, and for whatever reason it just doesn’t slip into your set list and pretty soon you know you don’t remember it anymore. I have my favorite hundred songs maybe that I wrote, but there are like three hundred of them, and there are a bunch of them that I couldn’t tell you how they go anymore.
